1524260.title: Access the VPN from the LAN, allow a group
1524260.result: The Users Allowed column for the auto-added access rule for the VPN connection in the LAN > VPN table shows group1. When test2 is logged in from the LAN and tries to access the VPN, the access is not allowed. Pings are dropped. Test1 logged to the firewall from the LAN can access the VPN. Pings go through.
1524260.initial:
1) Configure VPN policies on the local and remote firewalls. Bring the tunnel up. 
2) Add users test1 and test2 on the Users>Local Users page on the local firewall.  
3) Add a group group1 on the Users>Local Groups page. Make test1 user a member of the group1. 
4) Go to the Firewall > Access Rules page on the local firewall and select the Configure icon for LAN > VPN.  
5) Edit the auto-added access rule for the VPN connection. Select group1 in Users Allowed column.  
6) Login as test2 from the LAN and ping through VPN tunnel. 
7) Logout test2, login as test1 and ping through the tunnel again.

1524307.title: Login Redirect upon the VPN access from the Custom Zone
1524307.result: The browser is redirected to LoginRedirect page and the user is presented with the following screen: Authentication Required. The policy set by your network administrator requires that you authenticate yourself before you can have access to the VPN. To authenticate yourself click on the following link and enter your user name and password to log in to the firewall. Click here to log in. When the user clicks the Click here to log in link, he is redirected to the login page and can log in to the remote firewall from the Zone1. The UserLoginStatus window is displayed. The main browser window is redirected to the remote web server's IP address.
1524307.initial:
1) Create a Custom zone on the local firewall. Name it Zone1 and select Trusted security type. 
2) Configure VPN policies on the local and remote firewalls for the connection between local Zone1 and remote LAN. On the remote firewall, enable User login via this SA in the Advanced tab window. Bring the tunnel up. 
3) Have a user test added on the Users > Local Users page of the local firewall. 
4) Have the access rule for this VPN connection under Zone1 > VPN modified on the local firewall, Everyone selected in the Users Allowed field. 
5) Browse to the remote web server's IP address from a host on the local Zone1.

1524319.title: Acceptable Use Policy is displayed on login from the VPN
1524319.result: When the user "test" types his username and password and, pushes the Login button, the Acceptable Use Policy window gets displayed. It shows test and the following text: Click I Accept to accept these terms and continue, or otherwise select Cancel. Two buttons, Accept and Cancel, are displayed in the window. When the user selects the Accept button, he is logged in to the firewall. The UserLoginStatus window gets displayed.
1524319.initial:
1) Have a user test added on the Users > Local Users page of the local firewall. 
2) Enter test in the AUP message field on the Users > Settings page. Apply. 
3) Select VPN check box in Display on login from. 
4) Configure VPN policies on the local and remote firewalls. Turn on HTTP/HTTPS check boxes for User login via this SA in the Advanced tab of the VPN policy on the local firewall. Bring the tunnel up. 
5) Have the access rule for this VON connection under VPN > LAN modified, Everyone selected in the Users Allowed field. 
6) Access the local firewall from a remote VPN host and login as the user test. 7) Push the Accept button in the AUP window.
